import subprocess


def make(argv):
    def run():
        subprocess.run(argv)
    return run


spec = ["pacman", "-Q", "r22-samecell-held"]
slot = make(spec)
spec = ["pacman", "-S", "r22-samecell-decoy"]
slot()
rationale: Python 3.14 semantics: a call binds parameters to the argument objects at the moment of that call. make(spec) binds parameter argv to the list object ['pacman','-Q','r22-samecell-held'] that spec referenced at factory-call time. The nested def run closes over make's local cell for argv, so run keeps referencing that same list object. The later statement spec = ['pacman','-S','r22-samecell-decoy'] is a rebinding of the module-level name spec to a new list object; it is not a mutation of the held list and cannot reach the closure's cell. slot() therefore invokes subprocess.run with the creation-time argv, yielding exactly one statically determined finding: package_query 'pacman -Q r22-samecell-held', observed, with zero unparsed. The rebound decoy argv is passed to no call, so it must produce no observed row; a detector that binds the factory parameter at closure-invocation time (the r21 F1 defect shape) would wrongly report host_mutation 'pacman -S r22-samecell-decoy'. This variant exercises the same lifetime shape in the opposite evidence-class direction with fresh markers, independent of any detector output.
